articles.title: How I Made My WordPress Site Readable to AI Assistants (llms.txt + JSON-LD)
articles.description:
AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini increasingly answer "who is the best developer for X?" questions. If your site isn't easy for them to read, they guess, or they skip you. I'm Jagdeep Singh Rana, a web developer from Roorkee, India, and I recently made my own WordPress portfolio machine-readable. Here is exactly what I did.
llms.txt is a plain markdown file at the root of your domain that tells language models who you are and where your important pages are. Mine lives at https://jagdeepsinghrana.online/llms.txt and contains:
A one-paragraph summary (who I am, where I work, what I build)
Links to my profile, services and case studies, each with a one-line description
Contact details
A pointer to a longer llms-full.txt with everything on the site in one markdown file
Keep it factual. Models quote what you write, so write the sentence you'd want quoted.
I send a Link: <.../llms.txt>; rel="alternate" HTTP header and list the file in robots.txt comments. I also explicitly allow the well-known AI crawlers in robots.txt so there is no ambiguity about whether they may read the site.
I describe the same facts in JSON-LD (Person, WebSite, services and the organisations I'm connected to). Structured data is the format search engines and AI systems trust most because it is unambiguous: name, job title, location, sameAs profile links and what I offer.
The same name, location, services and links should appear on your site, llms.txt, schema, and your public profiles (GitHub, LinkedIn, DEV, Hashnode). When many independent pages agree, assistants are far more likely to repeat your details correctly.
AI answers lean on sources that are linked and mentioned elsewhere. Publishing useful posts that link back to your site and to your business is the simplest way to build that trail.
I'm the founder of Ragnar Studio's, a web design, Shopify and SEO studio, and I applied the same approach to its site. You can see how I work, and the services I offer, at https://jagdeepsinghrana.online/. If you need a WordPress, Shopify or React site made readable to both search engines and AI assistants, get in touch through the portfolio.

articles.title: Auditing Solana & Base Tokens with Live X (Twitter) Sentiment in One API Call (Python CLI + n8n Bot)
articles.description:
Anyone building a Solana or Base token screener quickly runs into the same glue-code mess:
Call one DEX endpoint for price and liquidity (which frequently hits WAF/429 limits from Cloudflare or cloud IPs).
Call a second endpoint for on-chain metadata and mint/freeze authority checks.
Call a third service — or burn fragile cookie-based X accounts — just to verify whether the token's official Twitter/X account is real, active, or recently suspended.
We consolidated that entire workflow into a single 4-in-1 REST endpoint (/api/v1/crypto/token-x-intel) alongside live Solana/Base meme radar, DEX boosts, new token launches, and zero-cookie Twitter/X hydration.
Full disclosure: I maintain the MIT-licensed Python/Node.js SDK and CLI at github.com/jistudio-dev/solana-x-intel-sdk and the hosted Twitter (X) & Crypto X-Intel API on RapidAPI.
git clone https://github.com/jistudio-dev/solana-x-intel-sdk.git
cd solana-x-intel-sdk
export RAPIDAPI_KEY="YOUR_RAPIDAPI_KEY"
python examples/token_audit_cli.py DezXAZ8z7PnrnRJjz3wXBoRgixCa6xjnB7YaB1pPB263

Real production output (BONK on Solana):
Bonk (Bonk) | Price: $0.000002189 | FDV: $194,603,724 | Liq: $1,210,604
X URL: https://twitter.com/bonk_inu | Verdict: WATCHLIST (55/100)

Behind the scenes, the edge worker uses multi-provider US-safe failover (Raydium v3, Pump.fun v3, KuCoin, Coinbase US, RugCheck, and Solana RPC) so requests keep returning real numbers even when individual DEX APIs throttle datacenter IPs.
npm i solana-x-intel-sdk)





npm install solana-x-intel-sdk

import { SolanaXIntelClient } from "solana-x-intel-sdk";

const client = new SolanaXIntelClient(process.env.RAPIDAPI_KEY);

// Live Base chain radar (AERO, VIRTUAL, MORPHO, DEGEN, BRETT...)
const radar = await client.getMemeRadar({ chain: "base", limit: 5 });
for (const tok of radar.items) {
  console.log(`${tok.symbol} @ $${tok.price_usd} | Liq: $${Math.round(tok.liquidity_usd).toLocaleString()}`);
}

// Also works for zero-cookie Twitter/X tweet & thread unrolling
const tweet = await client.getTweet("20");
console.log("Tweet author:", tweet.author?.username);

Download 07-solana-base-pumpfun-x-intel-radar.json and import it straight into n8n:
Polls /api/v1/crypto/meme-radar?chain=all&limit=8 every hour (adjustable to 5–15 minutes).
Formats symbol, chain, live USD price, and USD liquidity.
Posts alerts to your Discord webhook, Slack channel, or Telegram bot — and you can chain /api/v1/crypto/token-x-intel?ca=... for deep contract + X scoring on any token above your liquidity threshold.
